headline_marked: Rangpur: [[Four members of a teacher's family killed]], funeral rites held
headline: Rangpur: Four members of a teacher's family killed, funeral rites held
summary: Family members and locals expressed deep anger and demanded a swift investigation into the brutal killings in Machhuapara.
details: Funeral rites were held on Tuesday for the four members of a teacher's family who were killed in Rangpur city.
The rituals were performed according to Hindu customs at the the victims' home and a nearby temple in Machhuapara.
The event was attended by the Rangpur City Corporation administrator, Mahfuz un Nabi Don, along with people from various professions.
Despite the prayers for the souls of the deceased, family members and locals expressed intense anger over the brutal killings.
They demanded a thorough and rapid investigation to uncover the mystery behind the murders and bring the perpetrators to justice.
Administrator Mahfuz un Nabi Don urged citizens to provide any important information to law enforcement agencies to help solve the case.
He called for patience, stating that the police need reasonable time to uncover the actual mystery of the killings.
He also warned the public to be vigilant so that no individual or group could misrepresent the event for political purposes.
caption:
A family of four, including a teacher, was brutally killed in Rangpur. Now, their loved ones demand justice.

Funeral rites were held on Tuesday for the four members of a teacher's family who were killed in Rangpur city.

The rituals were performed according to Hindu customs at the the victims' home and a nearby temple in Machhuapara.

The event was attended by the Rangpur City Corporation administrator, Mahfuz un Nabi Don, along with people from various professions.

Despite the prayers for the souls of the deceased, family members and locals expressed intense anger over the brutal killings.

They demanded a thorough and rapid investigation to uncover the mystery behind the murders and bring the perpetrators to justice.

Administrator Mahfuz un Nabi Don urged citizens to provide any important information to law enforcement agencies to help solve the case.

He called for patience, stating that the police need reasonable time to uncover the actual mystery of the killings.

He also warned the public to be vigilant so that no individual or group could misrepresent the event for political purposes.

headline_marked: Up to 200,000: [[US to revoke visas of asylum seekers]] who entered as tourists
headline: Up to 200,000: US to revoke visas of asylum seekers who entered as tourists
summary: The Trump administration is targeting foreigners who used tourism or business visas to enter the US and then applied for asylum to stay permanently.
details: The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who entered the country for tourism or business but subsequently applied for asylum to stay longer.
The White House suggested that up to 200,000 visas could be affected, potentially making it the largest mass visa revocation in history.
State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott stated that obtaining a visa specifically to seek asylum is considered fraud and constitutes grounds for revocation.
This move is part of a broader drive by the Trump administration to reduce immigration and crack down on those who overstay their visas.
Since January 2025, approximately 175,000 foreigners have already had their visas revoked for various reasons, including criminal offenses.
The administration is also planning to expand the vetting of social media accounts for visa applicants to further tighten entry rules.
While some measures have been challenged in court, a federal judge recently struck down a ban on visas for nationals from 75 specific countries.
caption:
The US is planning what could be the largest mass visa revocation in history, targeting up to 200,000 people.

The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who entered the country for tourism or business but subsequently applied for asylum to stay longer.

The White House suggested that up to 200,000 visas could be affected, potentially making it the largest mass visa revocation in history.

State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott stated that obtaining a visa specifically to seek asylum is considered fraud and constitutes grounds for revocation.

This move is part of a broader drive by the Trump administration to reduce immigration and crack down on those who overstay their visas.

Since January 2025, approximately 175,000 foreigners have already had their visas revoked for various reasons, including criminal offenses.

The administration is also planning to expand the vetting of social media accounts for visa applicants to further tighten entry rules.

While some measures have been challenged in court, a federal judge recently struck down a ban on visas for nationals from 75 specific countries.
